amendments.change: added a 145x289 grid and evaluated the departure gate on it
amendments.reason: The first pass failed exactly two preregistered checks, both of them front-resolution checks: the flagship gave 6.5 radial and 7.0 axial points across the 10-90 front on the 97x193 grid against a preregistered bar of 10. No threshold is altered; the bar stays at 10 points in each direction. What changes is the amount of computation spent trying to meet it, which the preregistration does not fix. The resolution-stability check now compares 145x289 against 97x193 rather than 97x193 against 65x129, so it remains a genuine two-resolution comparison.

limitations: This is a resolved numerical continuation, not a proof.  Nothing here establishes or refutes a Clay singularity.

The departure gate measures distance to the Picard iterates of the *discrete* system on this grid; it certifies that the computation has left the linear-response regime, not that the continuous solution has.
Viscosity is fixed and positive in every run; no time-dependent or two-stage viscosity protocol is used anywhere.
